analysis:
Examined all supplied excerpts, patches and file metadata against the canonical index and detailed T-041 definition. NativeWorkerRuntime.swift:37-45 adds Gemma tensor-parallel dispatch, requiring equal shares, a data plane and no speculative/assistant policy, and forwards qualification and the owner's SSD key. Its added branches forward reservation, batch execution, cancellation, withdrawal, memory-pressure handling and shutdown; no omitted lifecycle dispatch or demonstrated authorization/encryption bypass is visible. Package.swift:79-85 adds an existing local qualification dependency only to TensorParallelCheck, not the worker target, without changing external dependency selection.

The actual documentation change at docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md:621 names Gemma4TensorParallelPrefix.scopes as another tenant-partition enforcement path. Surrounding text distinguishes cluster records from DBK3 and describes sealed scope, keyed filenames and disabled-cache behavior; unchanged no-salt fallback is not a new finding. Documentation alone does not establish these controls in the newly dispatched runtime.

Integration must examine Gemma4TensorParallelResidentRuntime.load and Gemma4TensorParallelPrefix.scopes: verify exact artifact/qualification and authenticated data-plane binding (TB-011, T-053/T-054), coordinator-authored tenant scope through resident and SSD reuse (T-041, A-001), key-unavailable behavior, authenticated restore, retention/storage limits, bounded multi-lane admission, cancellation and native retirement (TB-007, T-010, T-028, A-018). Those implementations and their callers are outside this batch, so their contracts remain unverified rather than observed missing controls. Reconcile cluster resident/SSD behavior with T-041's provider-tier assumptions without treating DBK3 policy as proof of cluster policy. No concrete regression is independently supported in this local source scope.
